metadata.case_name: CHENG MOK KAI AND ANOTHER v. LEE HING CHUEN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Fracture of the right Ulna (bone of the forearm)
source: He suffered a fracture of the right Ulna (bone of the forearm) on the 5th finger side. This was treated by operation and the application of a bone plate and bone screws.

injuries.description: Lacerations and abrasions with scarring (various sites)
injuries.body_part: back of right elbow; front of left knee; left loin; front of lower left abdomen; forearm (surgical scars)
source: He had a number of lacerations and abrasions. There are two small, ½in. scars on the back of the right elbow and two scars on the front of the left knee, a 2½ins. abrasion scar on the left loin and a l in. abrasion scar on the front of the lower left abdomen. Some of the scars are a grey colour but they will eventually become white and are of no consequence.
On examination there is a 5 ins. red scar on the forearm, the scar of the two operations. This scar will eventually become white and neat and of no consequence.
He had a fracture of the] right femur (bone of the thigh)... X-Ray shows that the fracture of the femur at mid-shaft is excellently united in good alignment.

injuries.description: Fracture dislocation of the right ankle
source: He had ... a fracture dislocation of the right ankle ... The fracture dislocation of the ankle was treated by operation on the day of admission ... X-Ray of the ankle shows that the medial malleolus i.e. the end of the tibia which forms the side of the ankle joint is united with some displacement and irregularity of the joint surface.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

source: He suffered injuries but did not have concussion, he was dazed and suffered from surgical shock. He had a fracture of the] right femur (bone of the thigh), a fracture dislocation of the right ankle and a fracture of the 4th left rib. The boy himself did not know that he had a fractured rib and this has healed perfectly and chest examination was normal.

manifestations.description: Ulnar Deviation: tilting the hand from the neutral position to the 5th finger side - this is known as Ulnar Deviation; it is 45° on the right and 55° on the left.
Slight weakness of fine finger movements although there is no loss of dexterity.
Reduced right hand grip: exercises a 55 lb. grip with the right hand compared with an 80 lb. grip with the left.
Occasional pain and discomfort persisting after the accident; pain during initial period and at operation to remove plate and screws.
1 1/8" shortening of the right leg (noted later as 1 1/8" and earlier described as approximately 1 in).
Deficit of 15° of bending the leg at the knee compared to the left (knee flexion deficit).
Ankle range of motion: right flexion to 90° and extension to 140° (left flexion 70° and extension 150°).
Marked limp; cannot run; plays only table tennis (previously played basketball, football, table tennis, badminton and swimming).
Gross muscle wasting of the muscles of the right leg (measurements provided showing obvious wasting).
Inevitable development of osteo-arthritis of the ankle joint in future (predicted onset around age 30-35, increasing impairment by ages 35-45).

treatments_received: operation with bone plate and bone screws (right ulna)

losses.description: Pain and suffering and loss of amenities; some inhibition in enjoyment of life and occasional pain following fracture and operations.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Prior to the accident played basketball, football, table tennis, badminton and swimming; now plays only table tennis and cannot run.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Lost one year's schooling and was left to repeat Form 1.
Pain and suffering and loss of amenities from multiple fractures and prolonged hospitalisation; ongoing and future discomfort from anticipated osteoarthritis.
